issues.issue: DMSA's right to retain existing and originate new media opportunities, advertising contracts and clients "for its own benefit" cannot be squared with c011's joint pursuit of the Business or with c015's diligent-efforts commitment. Which business belongs to the LLC and which to DMSA is left for construction.

DMSA agrees only that it "intends to use diligent efforts" to direct "appropriate business" to the Company — a statement of present intention rather than a promise, with no standard for what business is "appropriate." Prefaced by "without diminishing DMSA's rights under the foregoing language," it may impose no enforceable duty at all.

"Diligent efforts" is undefined and the clause supplies no benchmark — no quota, time period or measure — by which LSB's origination efforts could be tested. The asymmetry with c015's weaker "intends to use diligent efforts" sharpens the question of what standard binds her.

"Such services" has no clear antecedent — it may mean only originating media and advertising contracts and clients, or all services relating to the Business — and the restraint carries no geographic or temporal limit and turns on the undefined phrase "the Business." "LSB nor its principals" is also incoherent as applied to an individual.

"Dialogo" is ambiguous: c001 names the new LLC itself Dialogo, so the sentence either says the LLC will rely on its own staff or refers to LSB's pre-existing Dialogo publication. "Initially" also fixes no period and the sentence states no terms, cost or duration for the staffing arrangement.

The waterfall's second priority — repaying DMSA "the initial capital to launch the LLC" — is measured by c007, where that capital is whatever amount DMSA "deems appropriate" and includes DMSA's own staff labor and overhead. Read together, the two provisions may prevent any dollar from ever reaching the third and fourth priorities, contradicting c010's mandatory annual tax distribution.

"Any out of pocket costs" is unattributed: the clause does not say whose costs, incurred by whom, or whether board or budget approval is a precondition to reimbursement. The first priority therefore has no ascertainable boundary.

The restriction turns on "the approved budget," but no provision of this Agreement creates a budget, says who prepares or approves it, or provides for what happens before one exists. Read against c006's requirement of DMSA concurrence for all expenditures, the two spending controls cannot both be the operative rule.

The sentence is garbled to the point of unintelligibility — apparently addressing borrowing by the Board "if approved by" some unidentified body — so its terms cannot be determined from the writing. Whether the LLC may borrow, and whose approval is required, is unascertainable on the face of the provision.

The confidentiality undertaking covers all "efforts and actions" taken for the LLC in connection with the Business, with no duration, no exception for publicly available or independently developed information, and no definition of what must be kept confidential. Its breadth cannot be reconciled with the narrower, defined category of Proprietary Information in c024.

Disclosure is permitted with "the prior written consent of the LLC," but the provision does not say who may give that consent — the Board, the members, or an officer — and no other provision supplies the mechanism. The covenant also has no stated term or exceptions.

The definition is a closed enumeration with no residual catch-all, so items not listed fall outside it (expressio unius), while the last item — "client provided information, documents and data" — is unbounded and swallows the specifics. What is and is not Proprietary Information is therefore contestable.

This provision contemplates a later operating agreement of the LLC, and the executed Operating Agreement and Members Agreement contains an integration clause (Section 17.8) superseding all prior agreements on the same subject. Whether the Venture Agreement survives the documents it calls for is squarely presented.

The clause requires the further documents to be consistent with this Agreement and to contain "standard terms and conditions," a phrase with no referent or source standard. It is an agreement to agree whose content cannot be fixed from the writing.
